title: Shaktikanta Das's Call for Stronger Banks: Why Your Money is Safer
description: Shaktikanta Das, a key government policymaker and former RBI Governor, recently highlighted the importance of Indian banks maintaining robust financial reserv.

faq.a: Basel III is a set of international banking regulations developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) to strengthen bank capital requirements, improve liquidity, and reduce bank leverage, making the global financial system more resilient.

faq.q: Who decides how much capital Indian banks need?
faq.a: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the primary regulator that sets and enforces capital adequacy norms for all commercial banks in India, largely in line with the international Basel III framework.

faq.q: Does this focus on capital affect small banks too?
faq.a: Yes, capital adequacy norms apply to all types of commercial banks, including Small Finance Banks (SFBs). The RBI recently issued specific amendments to capital adequacy norms for SFBs, for instance, regarding their exposure to clearing counterparties.

faq.q: How can I check if my bank is strong?
faq.a: While exact capital ratios are complex, you can look for your bank's annual reports or disclosures, which often include their Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). Generally, a higher CAR indicates a stronger bank. The RBI also publishes reports on the health of the Indian banking system.

corrections.note: Corrected Shaktikanta Das's current role from 'former RBI Governor' and 'Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister' to 'current RBI Governor' based on verified sources.

edits.why: Shaktikanta Das is the current RBI Governor, not a former one. He was appointed as the 25th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in December 2018 and continues to serve in that role.
